title: POC sprint review — access & latency synthesis
summary: Weekly POC sync to review pilot onboarding, access gating, initial latency/throughput results, and next tuning steps. Discussed KV/prefix caching, batching, private VPC peering, and security checklist items. Agreed on bench matrix and owners for follow-ups.
transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2025-01-10
Time: 10:00 PT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Jordan Patel (Redwood SE), Asha Nair, Tom Reyes, Priya Singh, Ben Ortiz (BrightWave Health)
---
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone thanks for hopping on, is this still a good time?
[00:03] Asha Nair: yes, thanks Maya, we have Tom and Priya and Ben on the call, we'll try to keep this tight — got a bunch of infra work this week
[00:10] Maya Chen: perfect. quick agenda: one, access and creds status; two, share the early latency numbers Jordan ran on the pilot env; three, discuss caching/batching tweaks; four, security items and next steps. Anything else?
[00:18] Ben Ortiz: maybe one minute on canary routing — product wants a fallback plan if the model spikes latency
[00:22] Jordan Patel: noted, i'll cover fallback routing when i talk about batching.
[00:26] Tom Reyes: also, small thing — our traffic shape has many short queries (avg len 35 tokens) plus some long tails to 800 tokens, that's going to matter for batching and kv cache hits
[00:35] Jordan Patel: absolutely, we tuned for that shape — i'll show the per-sequence breakdown.

[05:02] Jordan Patel: ok first slide — quick reminder: this is running on Redwood Dedicated trial nodes in us-west-2 with T4-equivalent pools (note: the infra node labels changed during the run so some metrics map to pool-a vs pool-b inaccurately in the sheet)
[05:18] Asha Nair: that mismatch is what caused confusion in our infra dashboard, yeah
[05:22] Jordan Patel: right, that was my fault, i renamed a pool mid-bench. numbers: p95 generation latency at batch size 1 is ~220ms for the short queries, p99 around 480ms; for long queries p95 is ~1.1s. throughput with continuous batching set to 20ms improved tokens/sec by ~15% but increased p95 on short queries by ~40ms.
[06:00] Tom Reyes: hm, 220ms is ok but the product goal is 150ms p95 for short prompts. Is that realistic without changing models?
[06:10] Jordan Patel: two levers: 1) enable prefix/KV caching for repeated prefixes — you said many calls share common prompts — that can shave 40-80ms for short hits; 2) quantization to int8 on the model we onboarded — that lowers kernel latency but could slightly affect accuracy.
[06:30] Priya Singh: any impact on encryption or KMS when we quantize? Our security team wants assurance keys never leave the HSM
[06:36] Jordan Patel: quantization is model-level and runs in the inference runtime; it doesn't change key storage — KMS/HSM is used for transport and disk encryption of artifacts. but we will produce a security note for the SREs.

[09:15] Maya Chen: quick check — access status Asha? are the VPC peering and service account creds in place for the Dedicated trial?
[09:22] Asha Nair: we have partial. service account works, but VPC peering request is pending with networking — we expect it to be approved mid-week. also we hit an issue with our egress rules blocking the health-check pings, so some initial runs mislabeled nodes as unhealthy.
[09:40] Jordan Patel: that explains the earlier flakiness. for now we've set a fallback to hosted endpoint for read-only inference to avoid failing the whole pipeline.

[12:05] Tom Reyes: can you walk through KV cache behavior? our prompts have a 2–3 sentence standard intro followed by variable patient data — seems like a good candidate for prefix caching
[12:18] Jordan Patel: yes. K V cache — sometimes transcribed as K V — stores key/value activations for repeated prefix tokens. hits are perfect when prefix alignment is exact; with templated prompts you often get high hit rates. with our test set we saw 62% prefix hit rate which reduced mean latency by ~35ms on those calls. caveat: cache effectiveness drops with small perturbations in the prompt.
[12:45] Ben Ortiz: is that something we can make robust with canonicalization? we've got a templating layer that could normalize whitespace and punctuation
[12:52] Jordan Patel: definitely — canonicalization + checksum on prefix is the recommended pattern. Jordan: action item — i can share a small snippet to do checksum based canonicalization.

[15:30] Priya Singh: security questions: SOC 2 in-scope for the Dedicated nodes? audit logs available?
[15:38] Maya Chen: Redwood Dedicated comes with audit logs in the console; we can push longer retention as an add-on. SOC 2: yes we are SOC 2 Type II (note: internal doc says SOC two sometimes); we'll send the cert and the compliance pack.
[15:55] Priya Singh: and SAML/SSO? our vendor policy requires SSO + SCIM provisioning
[16:01] Maya Chen: supported, SCIM and SAML SSO are in the product; for private deployments we recommend connecting to your IdP directly — we'll share a quickstart guide.

[18:00] Jordan Patel: returning to latency — we ran a bench matrix across batch sizes 1,2,4 with and without continuous batching window at 0ms, 20ms, 40ms. short summary: batch=1 lowest p95 for short pulses, but throughput suffers. batch=4 increases throughput but short p95 goes up ~180ms. continuous batching window 20ms gave best tokens/sec with minimal p99 regressions for medium queries.
[18:30] Tom Reyes: so tradeoff is pretty clear. Product wants p95 150ms — can we hit that by changing batch/algo + KV cache hits?
[18:40] Jordan Patel: probable yes if you have high prefix hit rate (>60%) and you keep batch to 1 for short-path requests. Another approach is routing: detect short queries at the gateway and route them to a low-latency pool (smaller model slice) while routing heavy ones to larger pool.
[19:00] Ben Ortiz: that routing idea is interesting — what's the complexity to implement?
[19:06] Jordan Patel: it's a config change plus a lightweight inference proxy — Redwood's routing rules support header-based routing and heuristics out-of-the-box; we'll prototype a rule for length < 60 tokens.

[22:10] Asha Nair: checklist — who owns the prototype for routing?
[22:15] Jordan Patel: Redwood SEs will deliver a sample routing rule and an nginx-like proxy config.
[22:20] Maya Chen: i'll own the docs + example commit in your repo, and Jordan will run the bench for the routing case.

[25:40] Tom Reyes: one anomaly in the runs: a p99 spike at 2:14AM in the logs — looks correlated to a nightly backup job that saturated network egress. Any way to isolate that?
[25:55] Jordan Patel: yep we saw that — when network IO spikes the host scheduler can preempt the inference container causing tail latency. mitigation: set host QoS and separate backup VLANs or use egress shaping. we'll capture recommended network QoS settings in the runbook.

[29:00] Priya Singh: about data residency: can logs be filtered so that PHI never leaves our VPC? we need to ensure any telemetry is scrubbed before it's persisted outside
[29:12] Maya Chen: for Dedicated deployments we can disable telemetry export and store logs on your side; for hosted there are scrubbers and retention controls. we'll present the exact log flows and redaction options.

[32:50] Jordan Patel: demoing a quick bench -- reading numbers: run A (no kv) avg latency 280ms, run B (kv enabled) avg 240ms, run C (kv + canonicalization) avg 205ms; accuracy drop with int8 quantization was within expected bounds on our eval set (delta BLEU ~0.8).
[33:20] Ben Ortiz: 205ms is close, still above 150 — but if the canonicalization + routing to a short-pool hits maybe we're within range
[33:30] Jordan Patel: agree. also can explore model slicing or distillation to a faster variant. that becomes a product versus infra tradeoff.

[36:40] Maya Chen: security follow-up: Priya, you wanted specific encryption details and KMS flow?
[36:46] Priya Singh: yes, and a short write-up saying keys never leave KMS and that model artifacts at rest are encrypted with CMK. also need an attestable process for audit logs
[36:56] Maya Chen: we'll share the compliance pack and a short architecture diagram for KMS flows.

[39:10] Asha Nair: timeline question: we want to present a demo to execs next Tuesday, is that doable?
[39:18] Maya Chen: tight but possible — depends on VPC peering and networking fix. if peering is not in by Friday we'll use hosted fallback and show the routing + kv effects; if peering is on we'll demo Dedicated with real runbook.
[39:34] Tom Reyes: are there any blockers from our side other than peering?
[39:38] Priya Singh: SSO SCIM integration still pending but that's not required for an exec demo, it's for production onboarding.

[42:00] Jordan Patel: quick note on canary rollouts — we suggest a 10% traffic canary to the new model variant for a day and auto-roll back on latency regressions >20% or error rate >1%.
[42:12] Ben Ortiz: auto rollback is a must.

[45:00] Maya Chen: ok let's recap next steps.
[45:05] Maya Chen: Jordan will run the focused bench: batch sizes 1 and routing short-path then share CSVs.
[45:12] Jordan Patel: yes, i'll run batch=1, batch=4, routing short-pool, kv on/off, canonicalization on/off. target to share results by 2025-01-15.
[45:20] Maya Chen: i'll send the compliance pack and SOC2 cert by EOD tomorrow.
[45:25] Asha Nair: i'll follow up on VPC peering status with networking and aim to have approval by 2025-01-13.
[45:32] Priya Singh: i'll provide a short list of redaction requirements and any compliance blockers by 2025-01-14.
[45:40] Ben Ortiz: we'll prepare exec demo script and let you know if we need hosted fallback by Friday.
[45:45] Maya Chen: great, thanks all. any final Qs?
[45:50] Tom Reyes: none, thanks.
[45:52] Maya Chen: thanks everyone, we'll sync next week same time unless we escalate.
[48:00] Call ended

Notes about transcript: spoken language contains fillers and some words transcribed imperfectly ("K V cache" instead of "KV cache", "SOC two" instead of "SOC 2") to reflect typical ASR errors.
